Stop asking Bambu for its printer configuration bundle at startup

Every JusPrin startup sent api.bambulab.com a request for Bambu's printer
configuration bundle (slicer/printer/bbl), unless stealth mode was on.
JusPrin ships that bundle in resources/printers and copies it into the
data folder at every startup without the network; a downloaded one is only
offered through a notification. LAN printers read the shipped copy.

- PresetUpdater::sync() now reads sync_system_preset, as its other startup
  checks already do through the preset bundle it is given, and
  sync_printer_config() returns before any request when it is off. JusPrin's
  shell already turns that preference off (13c06c3ff3), so JusPrin no longer
  makes the request; OrcaSlicer users who leave it on see no change.
- shell_integration_harness --startup-requests starts with a person's
  settings (setup guide finished, stealth off, preset sync on), reads the
  app log until the startup sync reaches the bundle, checks it skipped it
  and sent nothing, then finds and connects the fake Bambu printer.
  It fails on the previous commit (the request is logged) and passes here.

OrcaSlicer-owned lines: 8 added in PresetUpdater.cpp (a priv flag, two
lines in sync(), an early return in sync_printer_config()); nothing deleted
or rewritten. sync_printer_config() is upstream behaviour (d8dd8fa634, on
upstream/main), still called unconditionally there.

Verified on Windows with a copy of a normal data folder and HTTPS routed
to a local listener: before, the listener saw CONNECT api.bambulab.com:443
and the log the request; after, neither, and the log says it was skipped.
With the fake printer on, FAKE001 is selected as a LAN machine and connects.

content.text:
JusPrin no longer contacts Bambu's server at startup. The fix is committed as `e9950ad3ee` on `claude/no-bambu-printer-config` (cut from `jusprin-newui`) and is not pushed.

**What was happening**
- **What triggers it:** shortly after startup, OrcaSlicer runs a background sync. One of its steps, `sync_printer_config`, asks `api.bambulab.com` for Bambu's printer configuration bundle. The only thing that stopped it was stealth mode. The preset-sync preference that JusPrin switched off in 13c06c3ff3 never reached this step. Your own data folder's logs show the request on every launch, answered in about 170 ms.
- **What it downloads:** a zip into `ota/printers` in the data folder. If it's newer than what's installed, OrcaSlicer shows an "update available" notification, and the bundle is only installed if the person clicks it and confirms.
- **Who owns it:** this is OrcaSlicer's behaviour, not something the fork added. This checkout's history starts at an imported root commit, so blame can't trace it here. Searching upstream's own history traced it to `d8dd8fa634` on `upstream/main`, and upstream still runs it unconditionally today.
- **Why local-network Bambu printers don't need it:** JusPrin ships the same bundle in `resources/printers`, and every startup copies it into the data folder without touching the network. The printer code reads either the shipped folder or that local copy.

**What I changed**
- I followed 13c06c3ff3's approach: JusPrin already turns the preset-sync preference off at startup, so I made this step obey that same preference.
- The change is 8 added lines in `src/slic3r/Utils/PresetUpdater.cpp`:
  - `sync()` reads the preference before it starts its background thread.
  - `sync_printer_config()` returns early and logs "skipped" when the preference is off.
- The preference has to be read when `sync()` is called. The updater object is created before JusPrin's shell turns the preference off, so reading it any earlier would see the old value. Reading it before the thread starts also avoids reading app settings from the background thread.
- Nothing in OrcaSlicer's code was deleted or rewritten. OrcaSlicer users who leave the preference on see no change.
- In JusPrin's own files, I only updated the comment in `ShellController.cpp` where the shell sets the preference.

**The test**
I added a new harness mode, `shell_integration_harness --startup-requests`. It starts the app with ordinary settings: setup guide finished, stealth off, preset sync on. It reads the app log until the startup sync reaches this step, checks that it was skipped and nothing was requested, then finds and connects the fake Bambu printer. HTTPS goes to a closed local port, so the test never reaches the internet.

**Verified**
- **Harness:** before the fix, the two request checks fail and the fake printer still connects. After the fix, everything passes.
- **Real app:** I ran `orca-slicer.exe` on a copy of `%APPDATA%\JusPrin2`, with all its HTTPS sent through a local listener that records each connection and refuses it.
  - Before: the listener saw `CONNECT api.bambulab.com:443`, and the log showed the `slicer/printer/bbl` request.
  - After: no Bambu connection at all, and the log says the step was skipped.
  - The only other connection in both runs was to `api.anthropic.com`, the Agent provider set up in that data folder.
- **Real app with the fake printer on:** it was selected as a local-network machine, `FAKE001`, connected, and sent its first status report.
- **Rebase simulation** against `upstream/main` `115df364e2` (base `3ffb9585d2`): `PresetUpdater.cpp` merges cleanly, the conflict list is the same with and without this commit, and the merged file keeps all three additions in the right places.

**Two things worth knowing**
- If a real Bambu network plugin is installed, the startup sync still asks Bambu whether there's a newer plugin. I left that alone because Bambu's local-network printers rely on that plugin.
- About a second after the fake printer connected, the app switched the selected printer back to the Anker M5. That's JusPrin reopening the data folder's last project, which uses that printer; it isn't caused by this change.

Logs and listener output are in `C:\b\nbp-evidence`.
